To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
some glutamate receptor subunits can form heteromeric complexes which are sensitive to both NMDA and kainate.
some CNS glutamate receptors are hybrid receptors containing both kainate- and NMDA- sensitive subunits.
some of the kainate-sensitive receptors in the CNS are hybrid NMDA receptors and that some of the NMDA receptors in the CNS contain kainate-sensitive components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, purification and reconstitution of the proteins responsible for mediating the excitatory amino acid responses of CNS neurones.
the molecular and cellular pharmacology of glutamate receptors.
the properties of glutamate receptors in vertebrate CNS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the protein isolated from Xenopus brain using a domoate affinity column is a mixture of kainate and kainate/NMDA receptors and that the RNA isolated from Xenopu and rat brain can express kainate and mixed kainate/NMAD receptors when injected into Xenopus eggs.

the protein isolated from Xenopus central neurones using a domoate affinity column is capable of forming channels which are sensitive to both kainic acid and N-methyl-D- aspartate and that the properties of these are similar to those of the channels which can be elicited in central neurones in vitro.
the evidence is consistent with the existence of hybrid receptors in the CNS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the protein isolated from Xenopus brain contains a mixture of kainate and glycine receptors and that the protein reconstituted from the kainate receptor fraction contains a mixture of NMDA and kainate receptors.
we have shown that some glutamate receptor subunits in the CNS of Xenopus and the rat can form hybrid receptors which contain both kainic and NMDA receptor subunits.

the protein isolated by affinity chromatography from the Xenopus CNS and reconstituted in bilayers is similar to a mixture of kainate and kainate-NMDA receptor subtypes expressed from Xenopus CNS RNA in oocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
some glutamate receptor complexes in the CNS contain both kainite-sensitive and NMDAR subunits.

the kainate receptors expressed in oocyte membranes and in Xenopus CNS have a high affinity for NMDA and that the NMDA receptors expressed in oocyt membranes and Xenopus CNS have some kainate sensitivity.

some glutamate receptor channels in the CNS are formed by a mixture of NMDA-sensitive and kainic acid-sensitive subunits, and that this mixture of subunits may contribute to the complex pharmacological properties of glutamate receptors.
